summary:
Our project is an educational space exploration game designed to help children learn about the Moon and life beyond Earth in a fun and interactive way. In this game, players take on the role of astronauts who explore the lunar surface and carry out missions to support a Moon Outpost.
Throughout their journey, players will collect resources such as water and minerals, explore the Moon's environment, and learn how astronauts could survive in a lunar outpost. They will also discover how plants, such as potatoes, could be grown in a controlled environment on the Moon.
The game will be developed using GDevelop 5, a game development platform that allows us to create interactive 2D games. We chose GDevelop 5 because of its user-friendly interface and features that support creative gameplay without requiring extensive programming knowledge.
Overall, this project aims to introduce children to lunar exploration, space technology, and the challenges of living beyond Earth. By combining entertainment with educational content, we hope to encourage curiosity and make learning about space more engaging and accessible.
details:
Following Questions:

Heyy, young leaders and change makers!! Have you know about our universe?? From distant planets to the vast surface of the Moon, space is full of mysteries waiting to be explored. But have you imagined what it would be like to live beyond Earth? How would astronauts survive, collecting resources, and even growing your own food? Sounds challenging, right?? So, would you be ready for the challenge?

Tools:


GDevelop is a free, open-source game engine that makes game creation accessible to everyone—no coding experience required. Using an intuitive, visual "event-based" system of conditions and actions, creators can quickly design, test, and publish 2D and 3D games without writing complex lines of code. Whether you are a student learning the basics of game design, a teacher bringing interactive projects into the classroom, or an indie developer rapidly prototyping an idea, GDevelop provides built-in art and sound editors alongside one-click publishing to web, mobile, and desktop platforms.

GDevelop is ideal for space-themed games because its built-in physics, particle systems, and ready-made templates handle zero-gravity movement and sci-fi visual effects right out of the box.

Headquarters:

Kopdes Washington is a virtual living space and main base in the game, inspired by the concept of Koperasi Desa/Kelurahan Merah Putih. It serves as the central hub of the game, designed as a residential environment with various areas and facilities to support everyday needs and activities. In here, we can feel save, save from any bad things from outside, we can breathe oxygen calmly and grow our own food so that we don’t starve. There is also a support system—such as computers—to monitor the surrounding area and protect us from threats, for instance, alien attacks or asteroids.

Not only that—we also give facts about rockys on the moon, such as Lunar Basalt, from volcanic activity some dark areas on the Moon, called maria, were formed when ancient lava flowed across the surface and cooled into basalt rock and also some of these rocks are rich in iron and titanium; Lunar Anorthosite, it was a light-colored, calcium-rich igneous rock taht makes up the bulk of the ancient Lunar Highlands, covering roughly 80% of the Moon's surface, it composed almost entirely over 90% of plagioclase feldspar. Lunar Regolith, it is the layer of fragmented, unconsolidated rock, mineral grains, dust that covers almost the entire surface of the Moon; the composition was it contain no organic material; the tichkness is about 4 to 5 meters thick in lunar mare regions and 10 to 15 meters thick in higher elevation; sharpness and dust, because the Moon lacks wind and water erosion to smooth out particles, it finest fraction under 1mm; exploration hazards, the abrasive, sticky dust clings to space suits. Lunar Water Ice, refers to frozen water (H2O) found on or beneath the surface of the Moon, the largest deposits of water ice are located inside deep, dark craters near the Moon's north and south poles. Because it never receive sunlight so the temperature can drop to extreme lows (around -248°C or 25K).

Impact & Benefits:

  • Learn about space: Discover planets, space objects, and fun facts.
  • Solve Problems: Learn to deal with obstacles and unexpected challenges during the journey.
  • Easy to understand: This could be easy for young leaders and changemakers to see and learn about space, because this cute game will bring you to explore the huge of our Milky Way Galaxy with interactive austrounot and element-element that we put.

Challenges Faced:

Enter a challenging survival adventure where your main goal is to survive for five days in an unfamiliar and dangerous environment. Every day brings new challenges that test your courage, creativity, and survival skills. You must complete important tasks such as planting potatoes to secure your food supply, fixing damaged cables to restore electricity, and overcoming your deepest fears as unexpected dangers appear along the way. Manage your resources wisely, solve problems, and stay alert because every decision matters.

Future Plan:


We plan to expand our game by adding more lunar locations, objects, and rover exploration missions to make the exploration experience more diverse. We also aim to enhance interactive learning by introducing more scientific fun facts, quizzes, and challenges about the Moon and space. In addition, we hope to develop the lunar life simulation by adding more outpost facilities, food production activities, and resource management challenges to help players better understand what it takes to live on the Moon. And we also hope we can expand our game not only exploring the Moon, but we can explore other planets and galaxy, but to make that we need lots of time and also lots of data from Nasa or other (like JAXA, ESA, CSA). Our vission and mission are, this project can bring good impact, can be part of our young future leaders learners, It can serve as a learning tool for our young, future leaders—a game that offers the experience of exploring outer space and our Milky Way galaxy.
